title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee, was arrested at gunpoint by US marshals in July 2025 and charged in North Dakota with four theft counts and four identity-related counts. She spent about six months in jail, including almost four months without bail before extradition and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud happened. She was released on Christmas Eve.

Lipps has sued the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck for $10m. She says Fargo police wrongly relied on an AI facial recognition system, which returned her social media photo as a possible lead, and that the detective requested an arrest warrant without enough investigation. The lawsuit alleges unlawful arrest, imprisonment, and malicious prosecution. A Fargo spokesperson said the city does not comment on pending litigation.
